challenge.name: The Consent Gap
challenge.description: A new model version requires loyalty basket data, but the deployment pipeline lacks the governance controls to verify consent. #automation_alex# wants to push the automated deployment forward immediately to meet the promotion deadline, while #requirements_reuben# insists on a manual review process to ensure legal compliance. #automation_alex# is open to adding a manual approval step if it keeps the pipeline moving, but #requirements_reuben# will not accept any automated path without full audit trails.

output.content: The promotion calendar is locked for the next three weeks, so we cannot afford a stalled deployment. I am willing to let the pipeline remain manual for this cycle. The extra hours spent on hand checking the consent flags will cost us in labor, but it is cheaper than the infrastructure bill for a fully automated audit trail. We accept the slower throughput and the risk of human error in the approval step. In exchange, we keep the deployment moving before the leaflet goes to print. This is a temporary concession to protect the margin on the middle aisle articles.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly accepts increased labor costs and the risk of human error in exchange for maintaining deployment speed and protecting profit margins, indicating a willingness to give up reliability for economic benefit.
